title: Brighton 5–0 Crystal Palace: three goals in ten minutes set the result
description: Final and half-time scores, the five-goal timeline and comparative match data first; analysis follows without repeating the logistics.

sections.heading: The result in one line
paragraphs: Brighton led by three inside ten minutes and added two after the break to beat Palace 5–0.

sections.heading: The decisive phase is visible in the timeline
paragraphs: The table separates Canvot’s own goal from Brighton’s four scorers. Gómez’s long-range goal and Ayari’s finish followed quickly: the early collapse mattered more than the final goal alone. Palace’s official report also records Mateta hitting the crossbar after the break; a missed chance is not necessarily a shot on target.

sections.heading: The shooting gap exceeded the possession gap
paragraphs: Possession was 57.2%–42.8%, while shots were 17–5 and shots on target 9–1. Brighton’s advantage extended beyond keeping the ball. Counts still do not measure shot difficulty, so without verified xG they cannot establish the scoring probability of each chance.

sections.heading: Passing and saves need their denominators
paragraphs: Pass completion is calculated from actual completed and attempted passes, rather than a rounded provider ratio. Brighton made one save from one opposing shot on target; Palace made five from nine. The own goal explains why simply subtracting five goals conceded from nine shots on target would produce the wrong save count.

sections.heading: What one emphatic win does not prove
paragraphs: The score and sequence support a convincing victory, but not a particular pressing mechanism. Interceptions and tackle rates depend on provider definitions and game state. Read them as observed match descriptions rather than a ranking of overall defensive quality.

sections.heading: Sources and unavailable metrics
paragraphs: The league page, both club reports and ESPN observations were cross-checked. xG, npxG, xA/xAG, PSxG, xT and PPDA were absent from the verified input and were not invented. The image shows actual half-by-half goals and score checkpoints through the last goal, not expected-goals or possession-flow curves.
